rows.note: Source facts: the Library of Congress country study reports Soviet support reaching $3 billion per year in 1990; its account describes military and economic supplies sustaining government forces against an active, fragmented armed resistance. The NDU history, printed pages 32 and 35, describes government forces and paid militia surviving with Soviet security assistance and losing their patron before the 1992 collapse. The 1989 US Department of State report establishes the armed resistance before the start date. Model assumptions: the annual 1990 estimate is an opening January proxy, not an observed January transfer. The existing Arms aid channel represents the mixed strategic supply package because it sustains force and charges the patron; this does not claim all $3 billion bought weapons. IdeologicalSecurity classifies this support for a Communist client as a programme authorized by the donor's opening governing bloc; a later AI government reviews that inherited commitment rather than all cross-bloc aid. That review rule is a game policy, not a claim that reform must cause a historical cutoff. Islamist is a coarse classification of diverse resistance organizations. Their military organization is not a vote share, population estimate or territorial-control percentage. No future cutoff, victor or date is encoded.
